1.explanation:
1. lighthouse-core/audits/critical-request-chains.js contains the audit logic that reads the network records, groups requests into chains by priority, and flags them in the Diagnostics panel. It’s here that the preload request gets classified as “critical.”
2. lighthouse-core/lib/dependency-graph/simulator/network-analyzer.js is responsible for assigning priorities to requests (marking rel=preload as high priority) and calculating blocking times. Its logic is why the delayed CSS shows up as a multi-second chain.
3. lighthouse-core/gather/gatherers/network-records.js collects the raw DevTools network events, including preload requests, which feed into the chain analyzer. Any change to ignore or re-classify preload links must happen where those records are gathered or passed along.
1.bug_scenario: When loading a page with a <link rel="preload" as="style" onload="this.rel='stylesheet'"> that points to a CSS resource with a long server delay, Lighthouse still flags that preload request as part of a “Critical Request Chain” and attributes the multi-second blocking time to it. In this test the CSS is empty and does not actually block rendering, but Lighthouse’s chain analysis still treats the preload as a high-priority, blocking request.

2.explanation:
• audits/critical-request-chains.js: This audit is responsible for reporting the critical chains. It doesn’t currently filter out preload-initiated requests, so it marks the delayed preload CSS as critical.
• lib/network-recorder.js: Collects raw DevTools network records (including priority). Preload requests arrive with “High” priority here and flow into the dependency graph unfiltered.
• lib/dependency-graph/page-dependency-graph.js: Builds the graph of request dependencies. No special logic strips out preload-only resources, so the delayed CSS remains in the chain.
• lib/dependency-graph/node.js & network-node.js: Define the graph nodes and their resource types/priorities. They hold the preload stylesheet node as a high-priority CSS node.
• lib/dependency-graph/simulator/network-analyzer.js & simulator.js: Simulate resource timing based on priority to compute blocking times. The analyzer treats the preload’s high priority as blocking, inflating the chain’s total blockage time.

To fix this, the audit (or one of these modules) must detect and exclude rel=preload requests (or reclassify their priority) so that onload-swapped preload stylesheets aren’t counted as render-blocking requests in the critical chain.
2.bug_scenario: A test page uses a <link rel="preload" as="style" onload="this.rel='stylesheet'"> pattern to fetch a stylesheet with a 5 s artificial delay. In Chrome the preload is fetched with “High” priority (but does not block rendering); however, Lighthouse’s Performance > Diagnostics > “Critical Request Chains” audit still lists the delayed CSS request as a blocking, high-priority item in the critical chain. This makes it look like the preload is hurting render performance when in fact rel=preload shouldn’t block the initial render.
